# Magnet Creates Pull Animation

## Problem statement

When the Magnet power-up (P9) is active, nearby power-up drops are pulled toward the ship at `MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED`, but the visual representation (the `graphics` object) does not update its position — only the logical `x`/`y` coordinates change. The player cannot see the magnet pulling power-ups in, making the effect feel invisible and unintuitive.

## Users

- **Players** — want to visually see the magnet effect: drops should visibly slide toward the ship along a direct path, changing direction when the ship moves.
- **Developers** — need the animation to be consistent with the existing simulation step (`tick(dt)`) and the current magnet attraction math.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to see power-up drops visibly slide toward my ship when the Magnet is active, so I can understand the range and strength of the effect.
- As a **player**, I want the pull direction to update in real time when I move, so the animation feels responsive and natural.
- As a **developer**, I want the visual position to stay in sync with the logical drop position used by the collection logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Visual sync:** Every frame, each drop's `graphics` object position is set to the drop's current `x`/`y` coordinates so the player sees the drop move.
- **AC2 — Direct path pull:** Drops within magnet range move along the shortest path toward the ship (already handled by the existing `_applyMagnet` logic computing `dx`/`dy` and stepping toward the player).
- **AC3 — Direction updates:** If the player moves while a drop is being pulled, the drop changes direction to follow the ship (the `dx`/`dy` calculation each frame naturally handles this).
- **AC4 — Existing tests pass:** The existing magnet test (`'applies the P9 magnet effect, and the magnet pulls a drop toward the ship'`) continues to pass, asserting `drop.x` moves toward the ship.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- The change must be minimal — touch only the visual position sync, do not alter magnet math, radius, or attraction speed.
- The animation must stay deterministic (same `tick(dt)` semantics — no frame-rate-dependent animation easing).
- No new Phaser dependencies or particle systems.

## Existing state

- `_applyMagnet(dt)` in `GymPowerUps.ts` correctly updates `drop.x` and `drop.y` each frame when magnet stacks > 0.
- `advanceDrops(dt)` updates `drop.graphics.setScale(drop.powerUp.currentScale)` but does NOT update the graphics position.
- `graphics.setPosition(x, y)` is called only once at spawn time — never during magnet attraction.
- The result: drops move logically (test assertions on `drop.x` pass) but appear stationary (the graphics stays at spawn position).

## Desired change

Update the graphics position each frame to reflect the current logical drop position. The correct approach is to add `drop.graphics.setPosition(drop.x, drop.y)` inside the magnet attraction loop in `_applyMagnet`, after each drop's `x`/`y` is updated — this ensures the visual position follows the logical position in the same iteration. An alternative is a dedicated `_syncDropPositions()` call after `_applyMagnet` in `tick()`, but the loop-local approach is more efficient (only updates drops within magnet range).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — Add `drop.graphics.setPosition(drop.x, drop.y)` in the `advanceDrops` method (or in the magnet attraction loop).

## Related work

- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** — Add a Magnet power up (GDD spec; completed).
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ** — Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math (completed; tests assert `drop.x` moves toward ship).
- **AH-0MTCO0M3C002Y67S** — GymPowerUps scene wiring (completed; implements `_applyMagnet`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** Keep to position sync only — do not add particle trails, glow effects, or easing animations. These are nice-to-have but belong in separate items.
- **Assumption:** The existing `drop.x`/`drop.y` logic in `_applyMagnet` is correct (it is tested and audited). Only the visual sync is missing.
- **Assumption:** Updating position in `advanceDrops` is the right place — it runs after magnet attraction and before collection, keeping the visual pipeline tidy.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the pull animation be smooth/eased or snap to the logical position each frame?" — Answer (derived from context): Snap to logical position each `tick(dt)` step, matching the existing deterministic simulation model. No easing or interpolation needed. Source: the codebase uses deterministic `tick(dt)` steps throughout.
- Q2: "Should any visual effect accompany the pull (particle trail, glow intensification)?" — Answer: Not for this work item. The operator's brief is about making the effect visible, not decorative. Decorative extras are scope-creep.

# Spawn power-ups in all combat gym scenes

## Headline

Add weighted-random, live-tunable power-up spawning (with random, enemy-avoiding placement and full collection) to the enemy-bearing combat gyms `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`, backed by a new general game-rules config and the existing pluggable `PowerUpSpawner` interface.

## Original request (verbatim)

> We need to spawn power ups in all gym scenes. There should be a plugable spawner. The initial implementation will simply pick a power up at random from all those available and place it at a random place on the screen (not on top of enemies). The frequency of spawn will be a configuation in the main game config file (if no such file exists then create a config system).

## Problem statement

The enemy-bearing combat gyms — `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` — spawn no power-ups at all, so a tester cannot observe drop cadence, placement or collection while under real enemy pressure. The three power-up/weapon gyms that do spawn drops use a hard-coded round-robin sequence at fixed screen positions with a compile-time interval (`POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL`), which does not reflect the intended in-game weighted-random behaviour (GDD §4.4) and cannot be tuned live.

## Users

- **Players / playtesters** — want the combat gyms to demonstrate power-up drops during genuine enemy pressure, so collection and effect behaviour (shield, bomb, phase, teleport, extra life, magnet) can be observed in context.
- **Game developers** — want a pluggable spawner plus a live-tunable game-rules config so spawn frequency and drop weights can be adjusted without editing scene code, and so the gyms reuse one shared implementation instead of per-scene copies.

### Example user stories

- As a playtester, I want power-ups to drop in the enemy and boss gyms so I can observe collection and effects while dodging real threats.
- As a developer, I want a live-tunable spawn-frequency control in the combat gyms so I can dial in the drop cadence without rebuilding.
- As a developer, I want the spawn ID selection and the spawn placement to be separate pluggable strategies so different scenes or difficulty tiers can swap either independently.
- As a developer, I want drop weights to follow the GDD rarity guidance (Extra Life rarer than standard drops) by default.

## Scope

**In scope:** `GymEnemies` (all archetypes) and `GymBoss`.

**Out of scope (already spawn, or enemy-free):** `GymPowerUps`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPlayer`, `GymIndex`. Converting these to the new random spawner/placement is a candidate follow-up, not part of this item.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` already provides the pluggable `PowerUpSpawner<T>` interface with `RoundRobinSpawner` and `WeightedRandomSpawner` (injectable RNG, runtime `setWeight`, equal initial weights) — the "pluggable spawner" seam already exists for ID selection.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` provides the shared grow → hold → shrink → despawn lifecycle and collection gating.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` (`EffectsRegistry`) tracks all active effects; `src/ui/HUD.ts` renders them (with a `showLives` option).
- `src/core/config.ts` is a localStorage-backed config system for `ShipConfig`, but there is **no** general game-rules config; power-up timing lives as hard-coded constants in `src/core/constants.ts` (`POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL = 12.5`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` is the shared base for `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`; it has a `Player`, enemy entities/bullets and a wipe→respawn lifecycle, but no power-up layer and no HUD/`EffectsRegistry`.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` is the reference implementation for combat-coupled collection (round-robin spawner, `EffectsRegistry`, P4 bullet clear, P7 teleport).

## Desired change

1. **General game-rules config** — new `src/core/rules.ts`, localStorage-backed and live-editable, mirroring the `src/core/config.ts` pattern (defaults merge, corrupt-JSON fallback). It holds the power-up spawn interval (default 12.5 s) and per-ID drop weights for P3–P9, defaulting to the GDD §4.4 rarity guidance (standard ~15–20 %, P8 Extra Life ~5 %, expressed as relative weights).
2. **Pluggable placement strategy** — new `src/powerups/placement.ts` exposing a `PowerUpPlacement` interface plus a `RandomAvoidingPlacement` implementation that chooses a random on-screen position (inside a margin) that does **not** overlap a live enemy body or the player, retries up to a configurable attempt limit, and then falls back to a deterministic safe position.
3. **Wire into the shared base** — `GymFormationScene` (covering both `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`) gains an optional power-up layer: a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 with the rules weights and an injectable RNG), the placement strategy, the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle, and drop tracking. One drop on screen at a time, next spawn on the configured interval.
4. **Full collection** — in both scenes, drops are fly-over collectible (≥ 3 % scale + hull overlap) and apply their effect through a shared `EffectsRegistry`; the standalone HUD renders active effects; P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets (no enemy damage), P7 is usable via S/↓ (nearest-safe-spot teleport + P6 on arrival), P8 updates the lives counter and P9 stacks.
5. **Live spawn-interval control** — a DOM-overlay slider (patterned on `GymPlayer`) edits the spawn interval in the running combat gym and persists it through the rules config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** A new `src/core/rules.ts` exposes a general game-rules config containing the power-up spawn interval (default 12.5 s) and per-ID weights for P3–P9 (standard IDs equal, P8 Extra Life rarer, per GDD §4.4). Values load over defaults and persist via localStorage, with corrupt-JSON fallback. Unit tests cover defaults, round-trip, partial merge and corrupt fallback.
- [ ] **AC2 (testing/validation):** A pluggable `PowerUpPlacement` interface and `RandomAvoidingPlacement` implementation in `src/powerups/placement.ts` pick a random in-bounds position that does not overlap a live enemy body **or** the player, retry up to a configurable attempt limit, and return a deterministic safe fallback when no free position is found. Unit tests with an injected RNG verify non-overlap given supplied enemy/player positions, the retry path and the fallback path.
- [ ] **AC3:** `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` spawn one power-up at a time on the configured interval, selecting the ID through a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 with the rules weights) and positioning it through the placement strategy. Scene-level tests verify the spawn cadence and that spawned drops never overlap live enemies or the player.
- [ ] **AC4:** Spawned drops use the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle and are fly-over collectible (≥ 3 % scale + hull overlap); collecting applies the effect through a shared `EffectsRegistry` in both scenes. Tests cover at least one collectible path per scene.
- [ ] **AC5:** Both combat gyms render the standalone HUD for active effects; P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets without damaging enemies, P7 teleport works via S/↓, P8 updates the lives counter and P9 stacks. Tests verify each effect is observable in a combat gym.
- [ ] **AC6:** A live spawn-interval control in the combat gyms changes the spawn cadence of the running scene and persists the value through the rules config; a test covers live application and persistence.
- [ ] **AC7:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse `PowerUpSpawner`, `PowerUp`, `EffectsRegistry`, `HUD`, `icons` and `audio` — do not fork existing implementations.
- Tests must be deterministic: inject the RNG used by the spawner and the placement strategy; never rely on the real render loop (drive scenes via `gameHarness`).
- The gym index and scene discovery must remain untouched — the shared base class carries the change to all archetypes.
- All written output in UK English.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "all combat gym scenes" means the enemy-bearing formation gyms `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss` only.
- **Assumption:** GDD §4.4 percentages are expressed as relative weights (for example standard = 4, P8 Extra Life = 1) rather than literal probabilities; the existing `WeightedRandomSpawner` semantics are reused unchanged.
- **Assumption:** "not on top of enemies" also excludes the player body, but proximity to the player is permitted (confirmed).
- **Assumption:** live edits apply immediately to the running scene; the next spawn uses the updated interval.
- **Risk:** adding an `EffectsRegistry`/HUD/drop layer to the shared `GymFormationScene` could regress existing `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss` behaviour — mitigate by wiring incrementally and running the full suite before review.
- **Risk (scope creep):** random placement + weighted spawning are also desirable in the three power-up/weapon gyms; this is recorded as a follow-up candidate rather than expanding this item.
- **Risk:** non-deterministic placement could make tests flaky — mitigate with injected, seeded RNGs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/rules.ts` — New general game-rules config (spawn interval + per-ID weights), localStorage-backed and live-editable.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — New unit tests for defaults, persistence, partial merge and corrupt fallback.
- `src/powerups/placement.ts` — New `PowerUpPlacement` interface and `RandomAvoidingPlacement` strategy.
- `src/powerups/placement.test.ts` — New unit tests for non-overlap, retry and fallback behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Wire the spawner, placement strategy, drop lifecycle, collection, `EffectsRegistry` and HUD into the shared combat base.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Extend with spawn-cadence, placement and collection tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Enable and configure the power-up layer per archetype.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — Scene-level spawning/collection tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — Enable and configure the power-up layer.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — Scene-level spawning/collection tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Re-source or alias the power-up spawn-interval default from the new rules config.
- `README.md` — Document the combat gyms' power-up behaviour.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Note the configurable/pluggable spawning for the combat gyms.

## Related work

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTE8EB6Q007EU0J** – Icons: code-drawn icons for P3, P4, P6, P7 (completed) — the drop icons this work reuses.
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed) — the shared base scene/archetype coverage added here.
- **AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM** – Thrust flame invisible on player ship; should scale with thrustAcceleration (completed) — unrelated, surfaced by keyword overlap only.

Also directly relevant (from manual context gathering, not in the automated report):
- **AH-0MTCPL9NA0025ZUI** – In-Game spawning should not be round robin (completed) — introduced the pluggable `PowerUpSpawner` interface and `WeightedRandomSpawner` this work builds on.
- **AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1** – Power-up core lifecycle + tunable constants (completed) — the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle and constants.
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** – Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) (completed) — the reference implementation for combat collection, P4 bullet clear and P7 teleport.

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — GDD §4.4 (power-up rarity/drop rates) and §6.4 (gym scenes).
- `README.md` — gym scene documentation (adding a new gym scene / gym descriptions).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — enemy gym implementation notes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope):** Which scenes are "all combat gym scenes"? — **Answer (operator):** "a" — the enemy-bearing formation gyms only: `GymEnemies` (all archetypes) + `GymBoss`. The other three gyms already demonstrate spawning. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (pool/randomness):** Which power-ups are in the random pool and with what probabilities? — **Answer (operator):** "b" — all 7 catalogue IDs (P3–P9), weighted per GDD (standard ~15–20 %, P8 Extra Life ~5 %) via `WeightedRandomSpawner`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (config):** Where should the spawn-frequency config live? — **Answer (operator):** "c (live editable)" — a general new game-rules config (e.g. `src/core/rules.ts`) that power-up settings join, live-editable (localStorage + gym controls). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 (collection):** Should drops be collectible with effects applied, or spawn-only? — **Answer (operator):** "b" — full collection with effects + HUD in `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5 (placement):** Placement constraints? — **Answer (operator):** "a + avoid spawning on player (near player is OK)" — reject only on overlap with a live enemy body or the player; retry to a limit, then deterministic fallback. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q6 (live-edit surface):** What should the gym control panel expose? — **Answer (operator):** "a" — spawn interval only. Source: interactive reply.


## Appendix: Plan session (Q7)

- **Q7 (plan approval):** Presented the 8-feature decomposition — F1 verification matrix & test fixtures, F2 game-rules config, F3 avoiding placement strategy, F4 base-scene spawning cadence, F5 collection + effects + HUD, F6 live spawn-interval control, F7 documentation, F8 full-suite verification & AC audit — with default weights (standard IDs = 4, P8 Extra Life = 1) and spawn interval = 12.5 s, plus dependency edges and test-first ordering. — **Answer (operator):** "LGTM" — the plan, ordering, dependencies and defaults are approved as presented. Source: interactive reply. Final: approved.

# Identify Enemy Refactor Opportunities

## Headline

Five regular enemy types (`Scout`, `Diver`, `Tank`, `Phaser`, `Swarm`) each extend `Phaser.GameObjects.Container` and share ~60% of their boilerplate (state management, destruction, VFX explosions, bullet creation, hit-radius calculation, aim-target pattern). Additionally, the `Boss` class duplicates audio helpers already present in `effects.ts`. This epic identifies concrete refactoring opportunities and creates child work items.

## Problem Statement

The five regular enemy classes duplicate large blocks of code across construction, destruction, rendering, collision, bullet creation, and explosion handling. This creates a high maintenance burden — any change to one pattern must be replicated across all five classes — and obscures the genuinely distinct behaviours (movement patterns, firing patterns) behind layers of boilerplate.

## Users

- **Developer**: wants to add a new enemy type or modify a shared pattern without touching five files.
- **Developer**: wants to fix a bug that exists in the same form across multiple enemy classes.
- **QA/Producer**: wants to be confident that a change to shared enemy behaviour is correct across all types.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All duplication patterns identified and documented** — a comprehensive inventory of duplicated code with file/line references.
2. **Child work items created** — one per refactor opportunity, each with clear goal, acceptance criteria, and files affected.
3. **Work items prioritised** — ordered by impact (lines-of-code saved, risk of regression, ease of implementation).
4. **No behavioural changes** — the refactor work items must explicitly preserve all existing behaviour.

## Constraints

- Phaser 3 game engine (Canvas/WebGL via Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics — no sprite textures for enemy bodies).
- No existing base class or mixin for enemies — all five classes inherit directly from `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`.
- The `Boss` class is architecturally distinct (4 phases, multi-graphics body, health bar, pulse waves) and is **out of scope** for the base-class refactor but in scope for its audio duplication.
- All existing tests must pass after each child refactor.
- The `enemyFactory.ts` and `enemyConfig.ts` infrastructure is a separate concern; this epic focuses on the entity classes themselves.

## Existing State

### Files

| File | Lines | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| `src/entities/Scout.ts` | ~280 | V-formation, aimed shots, wiggle movement |
| `src/entities/Diver.ts` | ~430 | Parabolic dive state machine, spread burst |
| `src/entities/Tank.ts` | ~320 | Rectangular formation, hold/move, radial burst |
| `src/entities/Phaser.ts` | ~350 | Orbital movement, radial 8-spoke burst, tell graphics |
| `src/entities/Swarm.ts` | ~340 | Cluster drift, coordinated burst, diamond shape |
| `src/entities/Boss.ts` | ~540 | 4-phase boss, multi-graphics, health bar, pulse waves |

### Key Duplications Identified

1. **Construction boilerplate** — Each class declares `bodyGraphics`, `explosionGraphics`, `explosionHandles`, `_alive`, `_shootEnabled`, `_lastFireTime`, config fields (`_size`, `_color`, `_bulletColor`, `_bulletSize`, `_bulletSpeed`, `_fireInterval`, `_shotProbability`, `_rng`) and initialises them identically.
2. **`_drawBody()` pattern** — `clear()` → `lineStyle()` → draw shape → `strokePath()`. Each is unique per type but the pattern is identical.
3. **`playExplosion()`** — Identical null-scene guard → `spawnExplosionParticles()` → handle tracking pattern in all 5 regular enemies.
4. **`destroy()`** — Identical teardown pattern across all 5 regular enemies: destroy graphics, iterate explosion handles, clear array, call super.
5. **`getHitRadius()`** — Nearly identical: `Math.ceil(this._size / 2 + HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX)` across all 5 regular enemies (Boss uses a fixed constant).
6. **`bodyVisible` getter** — Identical check: `bodyGraphics.alpha > 0 && bodyGraphics.visible` across all 5 regular enemies.
7. **Bullet creation** — Inline pattern duplicated ~20+ times: `scene.add.graphics()` → `fillStyle()` → `fillCircle()` → `setPosition()` → `setDepth(3)` → return bullet object.
8. **Aim target pattern** — `Scout`, `Diver`, `Phaser`, `Swarm` all have `target: Phaser.Math.Vector2`, `aimTarget` getter, `setAimTarget(x, y)` — identical interface.
9. **Boss audio duplication** — `Boss.ts` defines its own `getAudioContext()` and `blip()` functions that duplicate the identical implementations in `src/audio/effects.ts`.
10. **Config passthrough** — Each class accepts the same config fields (`size`, `color`, `bulletColor`, `bulletSize`, `bulletSpeed`, `fireInterval`, `shotProbability`, `rng`) with identical defaulting logic.

### Related Work

| Work Item | Title | Status |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN | Enemy Design tooling | completed |
| AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6 | Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide | completed |

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: Creating a full inheritance hierarchy (base class + mixins) could be over-engineering. Start with extracting the most impactful shared patterns first.
- **Boss is architecturally distinct**: The Boss class (4-phase, health bar, multi-graphics, pulse waves) likely should not share the same base class as regular enemies. It should be refactored independently.
- **Movement patterns are intentionally unique**: Scout wiggle, Diver dive state machine, Tank hold/move, Phaser orbit, Swarm cluster drift — these are the *differentiating* behaviours and should not be abstracted into a base class.
- **Testing**: Each child refactor must preserve all existing unit tests. The test files (`Scout.test.ts`, `Diver.test.ts`, etc.) will need updating if the class hierarchy changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — Extract shared base class, shared destruction, shared bullet creation
- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — Extract shared base class, shared destruction, shared bullet creation
- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — Extract shared base class, shared destruction, shared bullet creation

# Extract Common Enemy Base Class for Regular Enemies

## Problem statement

Five enemy classes (`Scout`, `Diver`, `Tank`, `Phaser`, `Swarm`) each extend `Phaser.GameObjects.Container` directly and share approximately 60% of their boilerplate. This includes: construction boilerplate (Graphics initialisation, config field defaults), destruction teardown, explosion handling, hit-radius calculation, body visibility check, aim target management, config passthrough, and formation position base calculation. Creating a shared base class would eliminate this duplication.

## Example user stories

- As a developer, I want a shared base class for regular enemies so that adding a new enemy type requires implementing only the distinct behaviours (movement, firing).
- As a developer, I want shared enemy lifecycle (alive, destruction, explosion, hit detection, formation positioning) to be handled in one place so bugs are fixed across all enemies at once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 - Base class extracted:** A `BaseEnemy` class is created that handles: shared state (`_alive`, `_shootEnabled`, `explosionHandles`), common config fields, graphics initialisation pattern, `destroySelf()`, `playExplosion()`, `destroy()`, `getHitRadius()`, `bodyVisible`, aim target pattern, and base formation position calculation (`computeFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, offset, spacingX, spacingY)`).
- [ ] **AC2 - All five regular enemies extend the base class:** `Scout`, `Diver`, `Tank`, `Phaser`, `Swarm` inherit from `BaseEnemy` instead of `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`.
- [ ] **AC3 - No behavioural change:** All enemy behaviours (movement, firing, visuals, positions) are identical to before.
- [ ] **AC4 - Boss excluded:** `Boss` does NOT extend the base class (it is architecturally distinct).
- [ ] **AC5 - All tests pass:** Existing test suite passes with zero failures; enemy-specific test files are updated if needed.
- [ ] **AC6 - Factory updated:** `enemyFactory.ts` works with the new class hierarchy.

## Constraints

- Each enemy still needs its own `_drawBody()` implementation (shapes are unique).
- Movement patterns remain unique per enemy — the base class provides `computeFormationPosition()` for the shared base calculation, and each enemy adds its own movement modifier (Scout wiggle, Diver state machine, Tank hold/move, Phaser orbit, Swarm cluster drift).

- Phaser 3 Container inheritance must be preserved (cannot use mixins if Phaser requires Container).

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` - Extend BaseEnemy

# Extract Common Formation Position Calculation

## Problem statement

All five regular enemy classes implement `applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, dt, spacingX, spacingY)` with the same base calculation: `x = baseX + formationOffset.col * spacingX + movementModifier` and `y = baseY + formationOffset.row * spacingY`. Extracting the common base calculation reduces duplication.

## Example user stories

- As a developer, I want the formation position base calculation in a shared method so that changes to formation geometry only need to be made in one place.

- [ ] **AC1 - Base calculation extracted:** A shared `computeFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, offset, spacingX, spacingY)` function or base-class method is created.
- [ ] **AC2 - All five enemies use the base calculation:** Each enemy calls the shared base and adds its own movement modifier on top.
- [ ] **AC3 - No behavioural change:** Enemy positions are identical to before.
- [ ] **AC4 - All tests pass:** Existing test suite passes with zero failures.

- This is a smaller refactor than the base class extract (child-3). It can be done independently or as part of the base class.
